messages:

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity questions for upcoming campaign

Hi Ben —

We're ramping a user-facing recall feature the week of Apr 5 and expect a short high-QPS window during the launch (peak sessions ~4k/min, average token length ~45). Can your Dedicated offering guarantee headroom for a 30–90s marketing-driven spike? Also, how do you handle burst billing and SLA when we exceed committed capacity?

If you can outline the operational runbook (what you need from us and how you plan to scale), that’d be great.

Thanks,
Sara

Head of Platform
QuantumAI

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity questions for upcoming campaign

Sara —

Thanks for the heads up — this is exactly the sort of scenario we design Dedicated headroom for. High level summary up front: yes, we can commit to short-duration burst capacity with predictable latency targets, but there are tradeoffs in billing and warm KV/LM cache behavior. Attached is a first-pass runbook and a spreadsheet with illustrative burst sizing (see attachments).

Key points:
- Baseline commitment: 8x H100 GPUs (pinned to your Dedicated pool).
- Burst path: up to an additional 8 H100s for 30–120s windows triggered by queue/backlog thresholds.
- Autoscale triggers: scale-up at GPU queue depth > 120 requests / GPU or p95 latency > 220ms for two consecutive 1-min windows; scale-down after a 5-min cooldown and sustained p95 < 180ms.
- Billing: burst usage is billed at the reserved rate + 40% on short bursts (applies to incremental GPUs only). We can discuss a capped burst credit for launch events under the deal.
- Quality: cold KV cache on new instances can add ~15–40ms p95; we recommend pre-warming policy for expected launch times.

Action items for us: Priyom will propose an autoscale policy and cooldowns; Laura will prepare a service-level exception for the requested launch window if you need tighter p99 guarantees. For you: final expected session ramp profile and any hard latency SLOs.

I’ll follow up with the detailed runbook (PDF) and the burst calc spreadsheet.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Dedicated capacity questions for upcoming campaign

Ben / Laura —

Putting a proposed autoscale policy here to iterate on. Summary: progressive fast-scaling with headroom cap and staged pre-warm.

Policy (proposal):
1) Pre-warm: 30 minutes before expected launch window, spin up +25% of burst cap (2 H100s) with KV pre-warm (simulate warm prefixes).
2) Emergency scale-up: if queue depth per-GPU > 100 OR p95 > 200ms -> add 2 GPUs immediately (scale step = 2). Repeat up to +8 GPUs.
3) Burst cap: hard cap at +8 GPUs above committed pool unless ops authorizes an overage.
4) Billing gating: if burst usage exceeds 10 minutes total in a 24h rolling window, trigger billing alert to customer success and sales (possible credits).
5) Fallback: if new pods fail to join or warm within 90s, route overflow to hosted fallback (model variant with smaller context) — requires feature flag and customer approval.

Notes:
- Cooldown: 5 minutes after last scale event with sustained p95 < 180ms.
- Metrics: queue depth, p95/p99 latency, GPU utilization, JVM OOMs, KV cache hit rate.
- Observability: 1s granularity metrics for launch windows; request-level tracing enabled for first 20k requests.

Thoughts? I called out fallback to hosted variant because we've seen customers prefer a graceful degradation vs. hard rejects during promo spikes.

—Priyom
